change_note: v0.9.6 (2026-08-05, owner-approved policy change, CAT-08 v2): accommodation nights are now DERIVED from the folio's check-in/check-out read by both extraction paths (schema items[].check_in / check_out), replacing the v0.9.2 employee-entered nights -- which was a self-reported divisor with no cross-check and therefore a gaming lever (inflating nights lowers per-night below the $300 cap). Nights = check_out - check_in, trusted only when both readers agree on the range (D3: a disagreement reuses blocking extraction_mismatch, no new flag). Fallback when the folio prints no readable stay range (D1a): a conservative nights=1 divisor, evaluating the cap at the smallest plausible divisor so uncertainty errs toward human review, never toward silently clearing the cap. apply_accommodation_cap no longer reads the deprecated items[].nights (retained additively in the schema for audit/back-compat). Schema gained optional nullable items[].check_in / check_out. Flag registry UNCHANGED at 16 blocking + 4 informational (D3 reuse). registry_version moved to 0.9.6 in lockstep. v0.9.5 (2026-08-03, owner-approved policy change): manager auto-approval visibility (APR-07, new). Every report that auto-approves is now included in a periodic manager visibility digest -- notify-only, no action required, does not change routing and does not delay payment. New config block notifications.manager_auto_approve_visibility (enabled true, mode digest, cadence weekly, action_required false). This is a control, not a review: it closes the gap where money left the company on a clean report with no named human having visibility, while preserving the design benefit that managers only ACT on flagged reports (30-40% of volume) -- the digest is visibility over the auto-approved remainder, not a per-report approval request. Delivery is a config-declared behaviour executed by the notification integration outside the scoring engine, exactly as payment batching is declared in the payment block without the decision engine running ACH; no orchestrator, schema, or flag change. Flag registry unchanged at 16 blocking + 4 informational. registry_version moved to 0.9.5 in lockstep. v0.9.4 (2026-07-30, owner-approved build): human correction re-evaluation wired into the real pipeline (VER-03/REV-04, previously documented-not-built). New INFORMATIONAL flag field_corrected records any human amount correction with the actor role (approver/employee/fin_ops) and the (AI value -> human value) pair for the audit trail and REV-04 label. The already-registered BLOCKING flag correction_mismatch is now emitted: an EMPLOYEE amount correction whose value equals neither extraction path (exact to the cent) routes to review. A human correction NEVER clears a pre-existing extraction_mismatch (anti-gaming: a disagreeing receipt still routes to a human no matter what value is typed); the human_value is authoritative and re-runs all policy checks. No config parameters added; flag list only. Flag registry: 16 blocking + 4 informational (up from 16 + 3). registry_version moved to 0.9.4 in lockstep. v0.9.2 (2026-07-27, owner-approved policy change): (1) new accommodation per-night cap -- accommodation_cap.per_night_usd $300 including taxes, flat across all cities in v1 (high-cost-city tiers remain a v2 enhancement, same as per_diem). per-night = folio total / nights (nights derived from trip length in v1, since the item schema carries a single date, not a stay range -- documented approximation, errs toward review when a folio bundles incidentals). Over the cap raises new BLOCKING flag over_accommodation_cap, which via special_approval_flags routes manager THEN S&TP; the overage is NOT auto-excluded (unlike per_diem) -- a human decides, since accommodation overages are often legitimate (sold-out conference city). Flag registry: 16 blocking + 3 informational (up from 15 + 3). (2) auto-approve ceiling raised: auto_approve_report_max_usd $100 -> $200 and approval_matrix tier-1 boundary $100 -> $200 (lockstep -- both define the same auto band), auto_approve_rolling_30d_max_usd $300 -> $400. A blanket flat-ceiling raise beyond this was rejected; per-diem/team/client/accommodation caps and all blocking flags are unchanged, so raising the ceiling only lets slightly larger CLEAN reports auto-approve. Per-diem scope reconfirmed (no change): $75/day covers meal_individual only; meal_group is the separate $40/head control. registry_version moved to 0.9.2 in lockstep. v0.9.1 (2026-07-23, owner-approved policy change): dual_extract_agreement_fields narrowed from [amount, date, merchant] to [amount, date] -- merchant is no longer part of the dual-path auto-approval gate. Rationale: after the OCR field-picking + preprocessing fixes lifted OCR accuracy on the domestic corpus, merchant remained the weakest agreement field (OCR merchant ~58% vs amount/date higher), so requiring OCR/LLM merchant agreement was the dominant cap on the straight-through auto-approval rate while NOT protecting the financial decision (merchant is descriptive, not the amount owed). A receipt where the two readers disagree on merchant but agree on amount AND date now auto-approves; a wrong merchant is caught by employee attestation + the 5% post-approval audit (PAY-03), not a synchronous gate. Amount and date still gate exactly as before, so accuracy-on-auto-approved for the money field is unchanged. extraction_mismatch flag and its routing are unchanged in mechanism -- only the fields it checks changed (see validation.check_dual_path_agreement, which reads this list). No flag/tier/schema change; registry_version moved to 0.9.1 in lockstep (equality pin, no flag change). v0.9.0 (CAT-07, 2026-07-21): new blocking flag date_unverifiable added to the flags array below (see flag_registry.json for trigger/effect) -- fires when an item has no extractable date, across every category, forcing manager review regardless of amount. 2026-07-17 (doc-only, no value changes): remaining non_reimbursable_line_types entries (minibar, in_room_entertainment, spa, gym, personal_items) confirmed as settled v1 policy on the same terms as alcohol -- no finance/HR sign-off gate for any entry, all auto-excluded identically, none routed to review. per_diem and team_caps/client_entertainment_caps values confirmed via business/HR/S&TP sign-off. v0.8.0 (PRD v1.6): alcohol added to non_reimbursable_line_types, confirmed live v1 policy (no sign-off gate). v0.8.0 (PRD v1.7, same-day follow-up): per_diem enforcement now aggregates across trip-linked reports (T10b) -- see per_diem.enforcement_rule; new blocking flag supplemental_report_after_trip_approval added -- any report for a trip that already has an approved sibling report is forced to manager-level review regardless of amount, to discourage drip-fed partial submissions (confirmed decision, 2026-07-16) -- 14 blocking + 3 informational flags now. v0.7.0 (PRD v1.4): Slack-only intake (email fields removed, deeplink intake is v2); flat $75 per diem with day-level auto-cap (high-cost tiers moved to v2); approval matrix re-cut to $2,000/$5,000 boundaries; payment process defined (AP file, Monday 23:59 cut-off, finance-ops release, day-10 SLA watchdog); per_bucket_label_threshold set to 500; manager_mismatch flag retired for v1.

pii_redaction.note: cardholder_name (GR9), drivers_license_number (DR3), email/phone (found during Phase 1 build, gated to rental-agreement-style context per DR4) added 2026-07-14. bank_account and digital_wallet_id remain listed but unimplemented -- deferred to v2 per DR1, zero real evidence in the 31-receipt corpus. Image-level (pixel) PII in real receipt photos sent to Claude vision is NOT covered by this config -- see redact.py module docstring and README 'Known limitations'.

per_diem.enforcement_rule: reimburse min(day_meal_total, max(0, meals_incidentals_usd - prior_approved_usd)); excess excluded; employee informed at receipt time; over_per_diem flag is informational
per_diem.trip_linked_aggregation: T10b (v0.8.0): day_meal_total aggregates across every report sharing the same trip_id, not just the current report. prior_approved_usd only accumulates from reports whose report_status is 'approved' -- a sibling report still in human review never suppresses another report's allowance (confirmed decision, 2026-07-16). Separately: ANY report for a trip that already has an approved sibling report -- regardless of whether the per-diem cap is actually breached -- gets the supplemental_report_after_trip_approval blocking flag, forcing manager review rather than auto-approval, to discourage drip-fed partial submissions. See policy_engine.py::apply_per_diem_cap and orchestrator.py's trip_reports registry.

accommodation_cap.note: v0.9.6 (2026-08-05, CAT-08 v2): $300/night incl taxes, flat (high-cost-city tiers are v2). per-night = folio total / nights, where nights = check_out - check_in read from the folio face by BOTH extraction paths (schema items[].check_in / check_out) and trusted only when the two readers agree on the stay range. This REPLACES the v0.9.2 employee-entered nights (which was a self-reported divisor with no cross-check -- a gaming lever, since inflating nights lowers per-night below the cap). D1a fallback: when the folio dates can't be established (folio prints no stay range, or a reader has only one endpoint) the divisor falls to a conservative nights=1, so the cap is evaluated at the smallest plausible divisor -- it never silently clears the cap; a genuinely over-cap folio still routes to a human who verifies the true dates against the image. D3: a reader disagreement on the stay range reuses the existing blocking flag extraction_mismatch (no new flag) and also falls to the nights=1 divisor. Bundled folio incidentals (parking, resort fees) still count toward the per-night figure, so it errs toward review, never toward silently overpaying; room-line itemization is a v2 refinement. Over the cap raises blocking over_accommodation_cap; via special_approval_flags the report routes manager THEN S&TP. Overage is NOT auto-excluded (unlike per_diem) -- approvers decide, since a sold-out conference city is a legitimate reason. The deprecated employee-entered items[].nights is retained in the schema for backward compatibility/audit but is no longer read by apply_accommodation_cap. Values set against 2025 citywide ADRs (NYC ~334, SF ~226, LA ~200, Seattle ~180; avg ~235) plus business-district headroom.

approval_matrix.description: Auto-approve if: total < $200, rolling 30d < $400, zero blocking flags, anomaly < 0.6 (v0.9.2: ceiling raised from $100/$300)
$100 up to and including $2K: Manager approval only (ceiling raised from $1K in v0.6.1; pending finance sign-off)
Above $2K up to and including $5K: Manager + Finance

approval_policy_note: S&TP is involved when policy is violated: any over_team_cap flag, any over_client_cap flag, any over_accommodation_cap flag (v0.9.2 -- routes manager then S&TP), or report total > $5K. S&TP does not review all reports, only policy-violation cases.

manager_auto_approve_visibility.note: APR-07 (v0.9.5): every auto-approved report is included in a weekly manager visibility digest. Notify-only -- the manager is informed, not asked to act; auto-approval routing and the payment SLA are unchanged. A financial control so money never leaves on a clean report with zero named-human visibility, without re-adding the per-report review load the system removed. Delivered by the notification integration outside the scoring engine (same pattern as the payment block); the decision engine emits no new field for it.
